alt: Question 1 on the major themes of the Qur'an (8 marks, set from the fifteen appendix passages) and Question 2 on its history and importance (14 marks) are compulsory. Candidates then choose two of Questions 3 to 5, set on the life of the Prophet and the first Islamic community, at 14 marks each.
caption: 1.1 and 1.2 cannot be avoided; the only choice is between 1.3 and 1.4 questions.

after: ## The major themes of the Qur'an
alt: Tawhid, the oneness of God, sits on top as the central theme. Beneath it are three further themes: prophethood, with Muhammad (pbuh) as the last prophet; the Day of Judgement and accountability; and guidance for individual and social conduct.
caption: Tawhid underlies the other three themes: prophethood, judgement and guidance.

after: ## The major themes of the Qur'an
alt: A comparison. Makkan surahs are generally shorter and more rhythmic and focus on belief: tawhid, prophethood and the Day of Judgement. Madinan surahs are generally longer and more detailed and deal with legislation and the organisation of the community, including worship, inheritance, marriage, treaties and warfare.
caption: The themes are not evenly spread: belief in Makkah, legislation in Madinah.

after: ## The history and compilation of the Qur'an
alt: After a strip on the Qur'an in the Prophet's lifetime (memorised and written, not yet one volume), two columns compare the caliphs. Abu Bakr compiled it after many huffaz died at Yamama, entrusting the work to Zayd ibn Thabit. Uthman standardised it after dialect disputes: Hafsah's sheets were copied by Zayd's committee, copies sent to the main centres and variants destroyed.
caption: Abu Bakr compiled the Qur'an; Uthman standardised it.

after: ## The life of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh)
alt: A vertical timeline split into the Makkah and Madinah periods: birth in 570, first revelation in 610, public preaching from 613, the Year of Sorrow in 619, the Hijra in 622, Badr in 624, Uhud in 625, the Trench in 627, Hudaybiyyah in 628, the Conquest of Makkah in 630 and the Farewell Sermon in 632.
caption: The Hijra of 622 divides his life into the Makkah and Madinah periods.

alt: Five groups studied in 1.4: the Prophet's wives, including Khadijah and Aisha; his descendants, including the line of Imams recognised among Shia Muslims; his leading Companions, the Ten Blessed, his Scribes and other major figures; the four Rightly Guided Caliphs in his lifetime; and the Emigrants and Helpers, formally paired on arrival in Madinah.
caption: Topic 1.4 is organised around people, not only events.
